_about: Cancellation of removal in immigration court (src/cancellation.py): the EOIR-42B for a client who isn't a permanent resident; the variant eoir42a (Form EOIR-42A) for one who is. Both are filed with the immigration court and served on ICE (OPLA), never mailed to USCIS (8 CFR 1240.20). Order: the G-28 that goes to USCIS (DHS's 'Instructions for Submitting Certain Applications in Immigration Court...', revised June 8, 2026, part B: with the two payment confirmations and a copy of the instructions), then the application, then the evidence the form's instructions (Rev. Feb. 2025, 3) ask for: the documents DHS issued, the qualifying relatives' status and relationship, the hardship, the 10 years, good moral character, taxes, criminal records. No cover letter: the court filing goes through ECAS or as the court directs. The attorney approves titles and order.
title: Cancellation of removal (EOIR-42B)
requires_message: The client hasn't been processed yet: process the client first.

handwork.text: Pay the EOIR-42B fee in the EOIR Payment Portal BEFORE filing, and print its confirmation page: one copy goes with the application, one to USCIS.
Pay the DHS biometrics fee ($30 a person) on pay.gov and print its confirmation page.
To USCIS, the lockbox for the client's state (the panel names it): the two payment confirmations, a copy of the signed G-28 and a copy of DHS's instructions. Nothing else goes to USCIS.
links: DHS's instructions for applications in immigration court

handwork.text: Two identical color passport-style photos taken within 30 days, the client's name and A-Number in pencil on the back (the EOIR-42B instructions, 6): one with the court filing, one with ICE's copy.
File the application and its evidence with the immigration court (e-file in ECAS in an eligible case) and serve a complete copy on ICE (OPLA), unless ICE takes part in ECAS; complete Part 10.

When USCIS's receipt and the biometrics appointment arrive: file the receipt with the court, and make sure the client goes to the appointment. None within 3 months, or the merits hearing within 6 months: call 800-375-5283.
Part 9 is signed only before the judge, at the hearing: leave it blank.
Every foreign-language document has a full English translation and the translator's certificate (the instructions, 5).

exhibits.title: The Notice to Appear and the court's notices
Documents DHS issued to the client: I-94, visa, work permit, USCIS notices; the passport
The qualifying relatives: their U.S. citizenship or permanent residence, and the relationship (birth and marriage certificates, divorce decrees)
Exceptional and extremely unusual hardship to the qualifying relatives: medical and school records, financial records, country conditions, declarations
Ten years of continuous physical presence: leases, bills, pay stubs, school, church and employment records, year by year
Tax returns and W-2s (the years in item 42)
Good moral character: police clearances from each place the client lived, letters from employers and people who know the client
Certified court dispositions and police records for every arrest (item 54)

leave_out.intake_questionnaire: The firm's own intake questionnaire: internal.
leave_out.g28: The firm prepares a new G-28 for the USCIS package.
leave_out.ssn_card: Not asked for with the application.
leave_out.drivers_license: Not asked for with the application.
leave_out.sij_order: Not evidence for cancellation of removal: the attorney decides whether it belongs.
leave_out.national_id: Not asked for with the application.

eoir42a._about: A permanent resident (cancel.form: EOIR-42A, INA 240A(a)). The EOIR-42A's instructions (Rev. Feb. 2025, 3) ask for the documents DHS issued, every criminal record, and what the judge asks for; no hardship test, so the hardship and relatives exhibits are optional equities. No photographs in its instructions.

exhibits.title: The Notice to Appear and the court's notices
Documents DHS issued to the client: the green card, the approval or immigrant visa, I-94, USCIS notices; the passport
Seven years of continuous residence after admission: leases, bills, pay stubs, school and employment records
Certified court dispositions and police records for every arrest (item 49)
Tax returns and W-2s (the years in item 41)
Family ties and equities: relatives' status and relationship, hardship, declarations
